name: basic-api-server
description: A script that creates a basic HTTP server with a few API endpoints.

promptLevels.beginner: make a simple web server that responds to requests
promptLevels.intermediate: create an HTTP server on port 3000 with two endpoints that return different responses
promptLevels.advanced: write an HTTP server that listens on port 3000 with a root endpoint returning "Hello, World!" and a /hello endpoint returning a JSON response
promptLevels.expert: Write an HTTP server that listens on port 3000. Implement two endpoints: 1) The root path "/" should respond with the plain text "Hello, World!" (content-type: text/plain). 2) The path "/hello" should respond with a JSON object containing a message property with value "Hello, stranger!" (content-type: application/json). The server should handle GET requests to these paths. Export the server instance so it can be closed after testing. {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use Node.js built-in http module. Include TypeScript type annotations for request and response objects. Use proper types from @types/node. Export the server instance.
languageInstructions.javascript: Use Node.js built-in http module. Create a server using http.createServer(). Handle routing by checking the request URL. Export the server instance.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use Node.js http module. Include JSDoc comments with @description for the main server creation, document the two endpoints, and use @returns to document what the module exports.

testCases.test: const http = require('http'); const server = require('./basic-api-server.js'); const options = {hostname: 'localhost', port: 3000, path: '/', method: 'GET'}; const req = http.request(options, res => { let data = ''; res.on('data', d => { data += d; }); res.on('end', () => { console.assert(data === 'Hello, World!', '/ should return Hello, World!'); server.close(); }); }); req.on('error', error => { console.error(error); server.close(); }); req.end();

const http = require('http'); const server = require('./basic-api-server.js'); const options = {hostname: 'localhost', port: 3000, path: '/hello', method: 'GET'}; const req = http.request(options, res => { let data = ''; res.on('data', d => { data += d; }); res.on('end', () => { const expected = JSON.stringify({message: 'Hello, stranger!'}); console.assert(data === expected, '/hello should return {message: "Hello, stranger!"}'); server.close(); }); }); req.on('error', error => { console.error(error); server.close(); }); req.end();
